terms.gloss: to be the object of (a verb), literally to be joined to it
terms.grammar: passive of adjungō, with the dative of the verb
terms.comment: Latin grammars of antiquity have no noun for the object. Where we say that a word is the object of the verb, Traupman says it is joined to it: hic homō verbō adjungitur (247), and Cui nōminī adjungitur? for a preposition, what noun is its object? (243). Traupman notes that the Roman grammarians never used objectum of a verb or preposition (247); we have not found the construction in Lewis & Short.

phrases.english: What noun is its object? — The noun “ōrīs”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 239, p. 243, p. 247.
